units: direct-tap units: the fitted cluster gains listed in direct_path (the AMPL-90 value is about 1.135, not 1; the absolute level is the fit's because the per-capture gains are fitted, so preserve the direct/reverb ratio rather than forcing the cluster tap to 1); delays in integer device samples from tap 0; mono in, (L, R) out; the input impulse at sample 0, tap 0 at sample 0
signal_path: input -> tap injection -> four parallel loops (filter G_i in the feedback, delay P_i) -> sum -> AP(20) -> AP(72) -> AP(230, damping b) -> output; the direct path (four taps per channel) adds in parallel. The reverb level does not move with AMPL; the direct path is x AMPL/90
measurement_side: not in this spec and not in the reference IRs: the 20 Hz-11 kHz analysis band (q1.LFBAND), the chain3 capture-chain kernel, the shared sub-100 Hz capture transfer (tools/lowband_joint.py), and the deconvolution's band-limit window on the direct taps. The plugin's own analogue chain (converter filters, sample-and-hold, 20 Hz high-pass, L half a sample late) is separate and follows this spec

value.ampl: direct taps x AMPL / 90; the reverb does not move with AMPL (S's linear cluster law)
value.onset: tap 0 at sample 0; the model's band-limited atom is measurement-side

value.format: a sum of signed impulses of magnitude `magnitude` at `delay` samples from tap 0, five per loop and channel (40 taps), added to the loop input
value.note: fitted, held out by RT; the same shape in every setting, scaled by one magnitude

injection.label: S (fitted, held out) / H (the physical injection)

value.form: y_i[n] = x_i[n] + G_i * (z^-P_i y_i)[n]; G_i is the loop filter in the feedback, stable, 0-3 first-order sections (shelf, gain, one-pole)
value.loop_filter: settings.<key>.loops[i]: gain, sections (exact form) and b / a (direct form, a[0] = 1); b / a already include the scalar gain, while `sections` do not; dc_gain is the total G_i(0); at_1khz is [|G_i|, arg G_i (rad)] at +1 kHz and excludes the z^-P_i loop delay; shelf(x) = (b0 + b1 z^-1) / (1 - pole z^-1) with b0, b1 from (dc_gain, nyquist_gain, pole) as model_s.shelf; onepole = (1 - pole) / (1 - pole z^-1)

ap230.g_note: use g (the model's FINAL_DIFF g230); the table file's g230 is provenance

value.form: all-passes in series, g = -1/sqrt(2); order immaterial (LTI)

value.hf_pole: one-pole at f_ref, T = 10^(-3 P / (fs RT) k (1/HF_e - 1)), HF_e = max(HF, HFRT_MIN / RT), p = min(p_law + c max(0, p_law - p0), P_MAX); the cells' hf_poles / hf_dp override p
value.dc_floor: g r0 >= DC_MIN; the cells' dc_min / beta / gamma and the folds' lfdc / hfdp / pramp / lfrt; the floor_form branch: dd = max(x, fd - c) + c exp(-max(x - fd + c, 0) / tau)
value.cells: analysis/loop_cv/hfcells_chain3_cap0.8475_apml/cells.json (dc, dc_min, beta, gamma, gamma_dc, hf_poles, lf_gain, lf_dc, or floor_form)

loop_filter_law.label: S at the library's steps / H between them (nearest RT fold, nearest sampled cell; the cells do not interpolate, §32.8)

AMPL.value: direct taps x AMPL / 90 (AMPL 90 = the reference); the reverb is fixed
AMPL.label: S

DELAY.value: a pure delay of the whole output; the library is all DELAY 0
DELAY.label: H

LOW_PASS.value: the panel's LOW PASS has no varying files in the library; response unknown
LOW_PASS.label: H

not_resolved: the LOW PASS response and its steps (no library data)
the law between the library's LF / RT / HF steps (H: nearest fold and sampled cell)
the direct taps' and injection's physical cause (fitted; S's AMPL is a linear cluster law)

references.note: device rate (the exact device_rate_hz; the WAV header is the integer wav_sample_rate_hz), float32, (L, R), input impulse at sample 0, tap 0 at sample 0, direct-tap units: use the listed fitted gains (the AMPL-90 tap is about 1.135, not 1). A port must null these sample for sample (float precision). They are the unit structure without the measurement band or capture-chain terms; the validation null is the reverb path only, because the direct taps' band-limited atoms are measurement-side

validation.simulate_scope: reverb path only: the direct path is substituted from q1.Joint.cluster in the check; the reference IRs use the exact taps and gains in direct_path
validation.simulate_note: time-domain simulate()'s reverb path against q1.Joint.render with the measurement band applied to both, reference settings, 0-1000 ms; the band and cluster atoms are library-side
validation.grid_note: production q1.grid_n(rt) gives Joint.render 2^16 samples (2.48 s) for RT <= 1.4 and 2^17 above, but this validation builds Joint.render on 2^22 samples so the check is not limited by its circular grid. The reference IRs come from simulate(), which is linear and has no such limit
